# Hound

> A small agent-oriented CLI and Python SDK for driving, inspecting, recording, and evaluating
> desktop applications without interrupting the person using the computer.

Use adapters for application-specific workflows. Hound selects only adapters compatible with the
current OS, leaves installed adapters editable, and supports JEV and CLEF System 1 drivers.

## Operating contract

- Use one adapter per application and edit it in place. Never create an adapter per step, modal,
  retry, or diagnostic attempt.
- Use a chain only when moving between applications.
- Foxhound already groups owned dialogs with their application and routes stage-relative input.
- A one-choice step runs deterministically. Zero JEV/CLEF calls is the ideal cheap path and still
  means Hound ran the workflow.
- Keep exploratory output in the Hound run directory. Produce one final tutorial video.
- After two failed exploratory runs, inspect evidence and revise the same adapter before retrying.
- Do not change Hound, Foxhound, or the app under test unless requested or a reusable defect is
  demonstrated by the evidence.

## Start here

- [Project and CLI guide](README.md): Installation, commands, adapter format, and evidence.
- [Agent operating guide](AGENTS.md): Minimal workflow and non-interruption invariants.
- [Example adapter](examples/notepad/adapter.yaml): Small complete Windows adapter.
- [Example registry](registry/index.json): Static `hound.registry/v1` shape; its repository URL is intentionally non-resolving.

## Machine-readable discovery

- Install globally with `uv tool install "hound-agent @ git+https://github.com/csaben/hound.git"`.
- Run `hound codex install` to add the optional global Codex skill.
- Run `hound codex remove` to remove that managed skill without touching other skills.
- Run `hound setup --json` to download and verify the pinned native helper.
- Run `hound check --json` to inspect local capabilities.
- Read `check.drivers`; when a needed driver is not ready, show its setup commands and have the user
  set secrets locally. Never request or place an API key in chat, an adapter, or repository files.
- For CLEF, start `hound clef serve` in the background (Node.js 20+ required). The first run opens
  a browser for the user to sign in to Cloudflare; poll `hound check --json` until
  `drivers.clef.ready` is true, then pass `--driver clef`. Never deploy the local proxy.
- Run `hound adapter-schema --json` for the adapter contract.
- Run `hound chain CHAIN.yaml --tutorial --json` for an ordered multi-application tutorial.
- Set `HOUND_REGISTRY_URL` or pass `--registry` before remote adapter discovery.

## Source

- [Public repository](https://github.com/csaben/hound): Canonical source.
- [Foxhound](https://github.com/csaben/foxhound): Native Windows backend and helper releases.
